title: The Hasse-Derivative Multiplicity Oracle: Characteristic-Free Exactness
description: The parent entry (factor-remainder-hasse-derivative-fq) and its first child (-oq-01) show that over a field of characteristic p the ORDINARY iterated-derivative multiplicity test is defective: exact only for true multiplicities m < p, and overcounting WITHOUT BOUND the moment m ≥ p. This entry answers the positive question those negative results leave open — is there a derivative-style test that reports the exact multiplicity in EVERY characteristic? Yes: the HASSE derivative test. Defining HasseCertifies f a n (every Hasse derivative of order < n vanishes at a — the divided-power analogue of -oq-01's OrdinaryCertifies), we prove hasseCertifies_iff_le_rootMultiplicity: for f ≠ 0, HasseCertifies f a n ↔ n ≤ rootMultiplicity a f, with NO hypothesis on the characteristic. The two-sided 'first nonvanishing order' lemmas (vanishing below the true multiplicity m, nonzero at m) yield the capstone rootMultiplicity_isLeast_hasseDeriv_ne_zero: for f ≠ 0, rootMultiplicity a f is the LEAST order at which a Hasse derivative fails to vanish at a — IsLeast, carrying no CharP hypothesis. Finally hasse_exact_where_ordinary_diverges places the two tests side by side on the same polynomial in characteristic p (any f with (X − a)^p ∣ f): the ordinary test certifies every multiplicity while the Hasse test stops one step past the truth; hasse_oracle_X_pow realises the contrast on X^p. 7 theorems, 1 definition, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

The positive resolution of the defect -oq-01 quantified for the ordinary derivative.

On any f with (X − a)^p ∣ f in characteristic p, the ordinary test certifies every multiplicity (from -oq-01) while the Hasse test stops exactly one step past the truth; realised concretely on X^p, whose ordinary test overcounts without bound at 0 yet whose least nonvanishing Hasse order there is exactly its true multiplicity p.

overview.historicalContext: The multiplicity form of the Factor Theorem says, over a field of characteristic zero, that (X − a)^n ∣ f iff f and its first n−1 ordinary derivatives vanish at a. In positive characteristic this breaks: over 𝔽_p, derivative(X^p) = 0, so the ordinary derivatives can all vanish while the multiplicity is large. Hasse's divided-power derivative was introduced precisely to repair the criterion in arbitrary characteristic. The parent entry pins the ordinary test's breakdown to a sharp cutoff at order p; -oq-01 quantifies the resulting error (exact below p, unbounded from p on). This entry closes the loop with the positive statement the negative results point to: the Hasse test is a correct multiplicity oracle in every characteristic.
overview.problemStatement: Is there a derivative-style multiplicity test that reports the exact multiplicity of a polynomial at a root in EVERY characteristic, and what is its precise form? Concretely: define the Hasse test to certify multiplicity ≥ n when every Hasse derivative of order < n vanishes at a. Show this test is exact — it certifies exactly n ≤ rootMultiplicity a f for f ≠ 0 — with no hypothesis on the characteristic, and identify the true multiplicity as the least order at which a Hasse derivative is nonzero at a.
overview.proofStrategy: Everything runs through the parent's characteristic-free Hasse criterion sub_pow_dvd_iff_hasseDeriv_eval_eq_zero: (X − a)^n ∣ f ↔ every Hasse derivative of order < n vanishes at a. Read as a statement about HasseCertifies, this is hasseCertifies_iff_pow_dvd. Composing with Mathlib's le_rootMultiplicity_iff (n ≤ rootMultiplicity a f ↔ (X − a)^n ∣ f, for f ≠ 0) gives exactness: HasseCertifies f a n ↔ n ≤ rootMultiplicity a f. For the oracle, pow_rootMultiplicity_dvd plus the criterion gives vanishing at every order below m := rootMultiplicity a f; and (X − a)^{m+1} ∤ f (since m+1 > m) forces some Hasse derivative of order < m+1 to be nonzero — necessarily the m-th, as all below m vanish. Packaging both halves gives IsLeast {n | (hasseDeriv n f)(a) ≠ 0} m. The head-to-head lemmas import -oq-01's ordinary_certifies_all_of_char_pow_dvd for the ordinary side and read the Hasse cap off exactness; X^p is handled via the parent's rootMultiplicity_X_pow.
keyInsights: The whole positive story is the parent's Hasse criterion read pointwise: certifying multiplicity ≥ n via Hasse derivatives is EXACTLY the divisibility (X − a)^n ∣ f, so composing with le_rootMultiplicity_iff makes the Hasse test measure the true multiplicity with equality — never an overcount.

Nothing here needs the characteristic. Unlike the ordinary value (derivative^[k] f)(a) = (k! : F)·(hasseDeriv k f)(a), which the vanishing scalar (k! : F) corrupts past p, the Hasse value stands alone. The capstone rootMultiplicity_isLeast_hasseDeriv_ne_zero carries NO CharP hypothesis — that absence is the whole point.

The true multiplicity m is the first nonvanishing Hasse order, split into two clean halves: below m every Hasse derivative vanishes (from (X − a)^m ∣ f), and at m it is nonzero (because (X − a)^{m+1} ∤ f must fail somewhere < m+1, and it cannot fail below m).

IsLeast packages the oracle in its sharpest quotable form: rootMultiplicity a f IS the least element of {n | (hasseDeriv n f)(a) ≠ 0} — membership is nonvanishing at m, the lower bound is vanishing below m.

The contrast with -oq-01 is exact and on the same polynomials: precisely where the ordinary test runs to ∞ (any f with (X − a)^p ∣ f, e.g. X^p), the Hasse test pins the multiplicity to its true value. The two children together are a complete negative/positive pair about the two derivative tests.

sections.title: Overview: the Hasse-derivative multiplicity oracle (characteristic-free exactness)
sections.summary: Imports and header docstring: the parent's defective ordinary-derivative test, the question, the Hasse test as a universal exact oracle, the main theorems including the IsLeast capstone, and why this is not a restatement of the parent.
sections.mathContext: This file (open question factor-remainder-hasse-derivative-fq-oq-02) resolves positively the question left open by the parent and its first child: the ordinary iterated-derivative multiplicity test is exact in characteristic p only for m < p and overcounts without bound for m ≥ p (overcounting_dichotomy); is there a derivative-style test reporting the exact multiplicity in every characteristic? Answer: YES — replace the ordinary derivative derivative^[j] by the Hasse derivative hasseDeriv j (the divided-power operator whose value omits the j! factor that collapses past the characteristic), giving a test exact in every characteristic with no hypothesis on p. Defining HasseCertifies to certify multiplicity ≥ n when every Hasse derivative of order < n vanishes at a (the divided-power analogue of OQ-01's OrdinaryCertifies), the header docstring (lines 1–71) states the results: hasseCertifies_iff_le_rootMultiplicity (exactness: for f ≠ 0, HasseCertifies f a n ↔ n ≤ rootMultiplicity a f, contrast OQ-01's certify-everything once m ≥ p); the two halves of first-nonvanishing-order (hasseDeriv_eval_eq_zero_of_lt_rootMultiplicity and hasseDeriv_rootMultiplicity_eval_ne_zero); the capstone rootMultiplicity_isLeast_hasseDeriv_ne_zero (rootMultiplicity a f is the LEAST order at which a Hasse derivative fails to vanish, no CharP hypothesis); and hasse_exact_where_ordinary_diverges / hasse_oracle_X_pow placing the tests side by side on f = Xᵖ. Why not a restatement: the parent's sub_pow_dvd_iff_hasseDeriv_eval_eq_zero (Mathlib) is a divisibility criterion with an order bound; the contribution here turns it into a pointwise multiplicity oracle (the IsLeast identification, the exact certified-value equivalence, the head-to-head against the unbounded-overcount regime), with the capstone's absence of any characteristic hypothesis the whole point. Research file, intentionally not registered in Proofs.lean.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) file of 170 lines, 7 theorems and 1 definition, settling the positive question the parent's negative cutoff leaves open. The Hasse-derivative multiplicity test is a characteristic-free exact oracle: for f ≠ 0 it certifies multiplicity ≥ n iff n ≤ rootMultiplicity a f, and the true multiplicity is the LEAST order at which a Hasse derivative fails to vanish at a — with no hypothesis on the characteristic. Placed against -oq-01, the two children are a complete negative/positive pair: precisely where the ordinary derivative test overcounts without bound (any f with (X − a)^p ∣ f in characteristic p, e.g. X^p), the Hasse test pins the multiplicity exactly.
conclusion.implications: This isolates what the ordinary test loses and why the Hasse refinement is the right fix: the ordinary value is the Hasse value scaled by k!, and only that scalar fails past the characteristic. Stripping it — the divided-power derivative — restores an exact, universally valid multiplicity test. Practically it is the correct primitive for detecting inseparability and repeated factors over finite and other positive-characteristic fields, where the naive derivative test silently reports arbitrarily wrong multiplicities.
openQuestions: Make the oracle computable: package rootMultiplicity a f as a decidable/algorithmic search over the finite range of nonvanishing Hasse derivatives (bounded by the degree), giving an executable multiplicity test valid over any computable field including 𝔽_q.

Transport the oracle to truncated jet algebras F[X]/(X^N), where only Hasse derivatives of order < N are visible, and determine the least truncation length N at which the least-nonvanishing-order reading still recovers the true multiplicity of a given degree-bounded polynomial.
